title: Constant-Rate Entanglement Distillation for Fast Quantum Interconnects
problem: Existing quantum interconnect protocols cannot simultaneously achieve high fidelity and high rate of entanglement generation under realistic noisy local operations, creating a fundamental bottleneck for distributed quantum computing and blind quantum computation. Current entanglement distillation methods either have vanishing rate or fail to tolerate the noise levels present in physical systems.
motivation: Fault-tolerant distributed quantum computing requires constant-rate, high-fidelity entanglement across interconnects, but all practical interconnect proposals fall short of this requirement, blocking the modular construction of large-scale quantum computers.
method: The work develops a constant-rate entanglement distillation protocol using a sequence of two-way entanglement distillation rounds based on quantum error-detecting codes with increasing code rate. The scheme combines these iterated two-way distillation protocols with standard fault-tolerance techniques to achieve a net constant fraction of the raw entanglement pairs being converted to high-fidelity logical pairs. Numerical optimization is applied to minimize practical overhead given finite memory constraints.
key_novelty: The first constant-rate (in expectation) entanglement distillation protocol for noisy quantum interconnects, achieved by chaining quantum error-detecting codes of increasing rate in a two-way distillation ladder.
contributions: Constant-rate entanglement distillation scheme tolerating noisy local operations, enabling high-fidelity quantum interconnects
Theoretical proof that the scheme achieves constant rate in expectation
Numerical optimization minimizing practical overhead under memory constraints
Demonstration of improvement over existing quantum interconnect methods for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing

metrics.other: Constant-rate entanglement distillation demonstrated analytically and numerically; improvement over existing methods not quantified with specific numbers in the abstract

baselines: existing quantum interconnect entanglement distillation methods
limitations: The scheme's performance under specific hardware noise models beyond the abstract's scope and the overhead of classical communication rounds are not fully detailed.
primary_theme: Constant-rate entanglement distillation for fault-tolerant quantum interconnects
